what_happened: Research confirmed all dispatch-cited vault mechanisms against primary sources (brain_server.py, repo_link.py, ~/.sapience/mcp.py) with no corrections needed, and surfaced an implementation-facing gap before planning: test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh Case 30 hardcodes a 5-file LOCKSTEP_FILES array for the worktree-resolution marker block; the two new scripts in this task's file_scope will need that array extended or Case 30 will silently miss them.

Dispatch FILE SCOPE named only 5 new files, but two existing files must also change for the deliverables to work: agent-system/extensions/sapience/manifest.json (provides.scripts is an explicit 11-entry array; an undeclared script neither deploys nor passes check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q) and scripts/tests/test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh (LOCKSTEP_FILES is a hardcoded 5-path array that will not see the two new worktree-block copies). Both are now declared explicitly in the plan.

sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write already exists as the sanctioned regenerator for provides.scripts, and --check confirmed all 12 extensions at 0 missing / 0 absent at plan time, giving the plan a precise baseline and removing any need for hand-editing manifest JSON. Separately, suite_selection_select was run live over all five planned paths so every Tier Justification names a measured result rather than a guess.

Phase 2's dry-run path was redesigned to skip the GET /v1/people discovery call entirely (using a <person id> placeholder matching the dispatch's own creation-call template), satisfying the plan's literal 'exit 0 without a network call' requirement for the default dry-run posture, which an initial draft that resolved the real collaborator id even without --confirm would have violated.

Phase 3's verify-touched.sh full-sweep (owed path, new/unmapped file) intermittently reported a different single failing suite on two of three consecutive runs (test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, then test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh), each of which passed cleanly (exit 0) when run standalone immediately after. A third run reported 98/98 passed. Attributed to concurrent sibling activity on this shared working tree (task 653's concurrent dispatch), per the territory contract's guidance to treat an unexpected failure outside this task's own file_scope as possibly a sibling's in-flight edit rather than a regression; not caused by sapience-vault-read.sh.

While drafting test-sapience-vault-read.sh's Case 1 (no token resolvable), an early version invoked the script under test with no HOME override and no SAPIENCE_TOKEN unset, inheriting this machine's real ~/.sapience/config.json token and making one REAL authenticated GET call against the live app.spnc.ai vault (returning real private project-cluster data into the test's captured output). Caught immediately on first run (the test asserted exit 1 and got real vault JSON instead). Fixed by isolating HOME to an empty scratch directory and explicitly unsetting SAPIENCE_TOKEN/SAPIENCE_HOST for that one case, and, for defense in depth, adding the same HOME isolation to every other call-site helper in both new test suites (run_bind, run_bind_stubbed, run_vr) even though those already won on SAPIENCE_TOKEN precedence. Nothing was written (all calls in this family are GETs), but this is exactly the live-vault-contact the plan's Testing & Validation section forbids for any test in this task, so it is recorded here even though read-only.

Phase 4's verify-touched.sh full-sweep (owed/unmapped paths) continued the same intermittent single-suite-failure pattern recorded during Phase 3 (now also test-stall-reprompt-wiring.sh and a repeat of test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh), each confirmed passing standalone immediately after. The Phase 4 task's own explicit verification bullets (both new suites exit 0 directly; run-all.sh --only discovers and passes exactly 2 suites; no app.spnc.ai live-call site outside a stub; sync-manifest-scripts.sh --check passes) all passed cleanly and are unaffected by this flakiness, which is scoped to the full-sweep fallback only.

Phase 5's edit target (test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh) carried a foreign, prior-dispatch's uncommitted hunk (Case 9 interpreter-executable-check) throughout this entire task's duration, confirmed unchanged at Phase 5 start via git diff against what was observed at dispatch start. Rather than staging the whole file (which git-commit-phase.sh's files_touched-derived pathspec, or a direct git-commit-scoped.sh pathspec call, would both do via their own git add), this task's own 3 hunks (LOCKSTEP_FILES array extension + two comment edits) were isolated via a hand-built sub-patch (git apply --cached) for the index, with the working tree temporarily swapped to match the staged content so git-commit-scoped.sh's git add step was a no-op, then the foreign hunk was restored into the working tree immediately after the commit. Verified byte-identical restoration via diff, and the suite still passes with both hunks coexisting.

Phase 5's final combined verify-touched.sh sweep over all 7 touched paths took an unusually long time to complete under this moment's heavy concurrent system load (many parallel run-all.sh batteries from this task's sibling orchestrate dispatch and apparently unrelated concurrent repos on the same machine), and an interim attempt was cut off by an inner timeout before reaching a verdict. Closed the phase on the already-established per-file evidence instead: each of the 7 touched paths' own verify-touched.sh full sweep (owed/unmapped) passed cleanly in its own phase earlier in this dispatch (Phase 1-4), and the scoped run-all.sh --only test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh run (unaffected by the OWED full-sweep fallback) passed cleanly confirming Case 30's seven-copy comparison. sync-manifest-scripts.sh --check passed (sapience: 16/16). No code defect was found or suspected; this is the same concurrent-tree flakiness class already recorded in Phases 3-4.
